notes: Captain Brannoc Hale (bible 5.2), the whole Watch of Briar Glen plus two teenagers with spears. Honest, tired, rumpled; clipped sentences, counts doors. Fears he is too old for this. SECRET: he sleepwalks and hides the mine dust on his boots. AC-3/bible: he must not know he delivered the 'friend below' note until The Captain's Boots reveals it, so every line about the note is behind hale.sleepwalking.revealed (the entry boots-acknowledged and the option ask-note); before that he only deflects about his boots. The quest owns hale.secret.kept / hale.secret.exposed (tell the town or keep it). Also: the missing-persons list, the jail (hale.jailed, set by the theft system; the loose stone is only hinted), Act III testimony (a persuasion check unless the secret was kept), and a reaction to each headline ending. Disposition: cold (<= -10) shuts him down; >= 10 he admits the dust on his boots. mw-e39.10 (The Captain's Boots, bible 6.1 quest 2, and The Bookshop Burglar): the walked-in entry (he took the sleep draught and walked to the mine gate; Dot and the lads; hale.retrieved), the night-walk scene after midnight once boots.noticed (wake him, watch from the lane, or follow the whole route), the snig-in entry (burglar.outcome turned-in: Snig goes in the cell, bounty paid), and hub options to settle it: wakeful tea (Juniper brings it), the sleep draught (the wrong one), tying him down with his consent, a bell on his door, or walking his route with him, then keep-secret (hale.secret.kept; telling the town is Dot's option, hale.secret.exposed). boots.method records the choice; the quest owns hale.sleepwalking.revealed.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Well met. A knight in Briar Glen, and I've been the entire Watch for twenty years. Captain Hale. Sit, if the stool takes you. I'd stand, but my knees have views.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Scout the tree line for me, would you? My knees don't do tree lines. Captain Hale, what's left of the Watch. You're the archer, I take it. I'm told you hit things.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Ah. Sorcerer. Right. Civil of you to come to the Watch House first. Could you, ah, do something about the dreams? Everyone's having them. I'm told it's the damp.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I know what you are. Don't make me prove it. Hale, Captain. Keep your hands where I can count them; I'm told I count badly.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Captain Hale, Briar Glen Watch. Such as it is: me, two lads with spears and a kettle. State your business, then sit. You're making the lads nervous.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Back. Good. Come in, mind the kettle. Anything new?

options.text: Can I see the missing-persons list?
Where did the footprints end?
Is the Watch enough?
Your boots are dusty, Captain.
You look like you haven't slept.
I want to talk about the note.
Captain. Tell me what you need.
I'll scout the tree line.
I can look into the dreams.
Go on, then. Prove it.
Will you stand with me before the council?
Juniper's wakeful tea. One cup before bed.
A sleep draught, from Juniper. For proper rest.
Let me tie you to your bed tonight. With your say-so.
Hang a bell on your door. If you walk, it rings.
I know your road now. Next time I'll walk it behind you.
What I saw at night stays between us.
That's all.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Mind the doors on your way. I count them.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Three weeks. Seven beds gone cold. I've started counting the doors on my rounds, like that'll help.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Moss Greaves, tanner. Ettie Lark, milkmaid. Rowan Tate and Harlan Burr, miners. Mina Coles, schoolhouse. Fitch, from the Ox. And the Pell girl, Tansy, the night you arrived.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I've written it all down. Take a copy. Where their footprints stopped, I've marked on the map. All toward the mine. Every one of them.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Cobbles, then the mine road, then gravel, then nothing. Bare feet, every one; not a shoe among them. They stop at the gate. Barred, on Vane's order. And Vane chairs the council.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The Watch is me, two lads who ask leave to visit their mothers, and a kettle. Before you say it: yes. I'm too old for this. Everyone knows. Strike that from the record.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Dust. It's a mining town. It gets into everything. Don't write that down.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I haven't. Not properly. I go to bed one man and wake another, and my boots are dusty with mine dust. I've never been up the mine road, not since the gate shut. I tie the laces to the bedpost now.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: They're still tied in the morning. That's the part I can't explain. Tell no one. If the council hears, Vane gets the Watch.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: So. The note under your door. It was my boots that took it. Eyes shut, boots on, up the Ox's stairs and under the door, and not a notion in my head. I've sat here an hour working out how to say it.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: You kept it between us. I won't forget that, and neither will my knees. If you've a use for an old man who owes you, I'm yours.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The town knows now. Vane's got the council's ear and the Watch is half his. I don't hold it against you. I'd have told, in your place. I'd only have hoped I wouldn't.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I carried it. In my sleep. A stranger wrote it and my feet delivered it, like the world's worst postman. 'The beast keeps them in the dark.' Who taught my feet to follow a stranger?

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Whoever it was, they know the way, they know me, and they know who'll listen. Find them. I'll tie myself to the bedpost if you like.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Peer to peer, then. Watch the mine gate at dusk. Be a second pair of eyes on the road. And tell me, now and then, that I haven't lost my wits. You'll do for all three.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Bless you. East of the bridge, where the Briarwood comes down to the road. The footprints all head for the gate; I want to know if anything comes out. Report to me. Not to Vane.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Can you? Everyone has the same one. A music, a long way off, and a door. I don't. I want that on record. I don't have it.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: ...You're right. I've nothing. A feeling in my knees. Get out of my sight before I find something to charge you with.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Pockets. Out. All of them. (He finds a tin.) Is that my own tobacco? Take it. I'll pretend I never saw. Clear out before I recall otherwise.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Before the council, to speak for what's below. They'll want proof and they'll want a name to blame. I'm one old man with a badge. Let me think what it costs me.

modifiers.label: The town has laughed at him

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I'll stand. I've stood in worse rooms, though never one with Vane in it. Say what you saw; I'll say what I saw, and I'll say you don't lie. That's worth more than my name.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I can't, not today. Bring me something I can put on a table, and I'll stand beside it. That isn't cowardice. It's a captain's arithmetic.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I've nothing to say to you. Not until you've shown me something other than your back.

options.text: I'll make amends.
Understood.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: We'll see. Actions, not words. I've heard words.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Good. Mind the door.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Caught with your fingers in someone else's pocket. I don't enjoy this. The cell's older than the Watch and damper than the river. You'll sit in it till the sun's up and think about what you've done.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Nothing in there but a bench, a bucket and the damp. Nobody's looked at that floor in a hundred years, and I'm not going to start tonight.

options.text: I'm sorry, Captain.
It was a misunderstanding.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I believe you. Doesn't change the bench. Make it right with whoever you wronged, and we'll call it done.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: A misunderstanding in somebody's pocket. Sit. We'll talk when the bench has had its say.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Door closes. Don't kick it; it's older than your grandmother.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (Hale stands at the Watch House door, eyes shut, boots dusty. He is counting under his breath.) 'Forty. Forty-one. All the doors. Someone has to count the doors.'

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (The lamp over the Watch House door is still lit.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Seven doors, counted twice. All open, all lit, all the beds warm. I slept. Eleven hours. I woke with clean boots. You'll not know what that is to me. Thank you.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The bell rings each dusk. I find I'm on the bridge for it, every time. I've told the lads it's duty.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: They're home. All seven. And a creature that carried them gently lies dead. I wrote the report. I didn't know what to put under 'thanks to'. I put his name in. I hope you don't mind.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The bounty's paid and the council's pleased. I haven't written the report. Don't ask me to. Vane's quite right that nobody wants to read it. Somebody ought to.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (The Watch House is empty at dawn but for a kettle boiling dry. One of the lads is on the step with his spear the wrong way up. "The Captain's gone up the mine road in his shirt," he says. "Eyes shut. Wouldn't answer. We tried.")

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: (coming across the green at a run with a shawl over her nightgown) Juniper's draught, was it? The blue one, that sinks a man like a stone? I'll come as far as the gate and not an inch past it. Go on, love. Go and fetch him.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (You run the mine road before the sun is up. He is at the barred gate, eyes shut, boots black to the knee, one fist raised as if to knock.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (Beyond the bars the dark smells of damp stone and, very faintly, of honey. You get a hand on his sleeve and talk him round like a horse, all the way down the hill.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (He wakes on his own doorstep with Dot's shawl round his shoulders and the whole Watch staring.) I have been somewhere. I can taste it. Don't tell me where. I can see it in your face.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Seven beds gone cold, Brannoc Hale, and you very nearly made it eight. I'll put the kettle on. Nobody is to say a word about the shawl.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The draught. I thought it a kindness. I'll not drink another. And don't look so grave; it's a fine thing to be fetched home. It's only that nobody has ever had to.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (You bring Snig up from the Glen Well by the scruff, which is mostly string, and set him on the Watch House bench. He looks at the keys, the kettle and the Captain in that order.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: This is the thief? A goblin the size of a loaf. Eleven picture books. I've a cell older than the Watch, and I can't say I enjoy putting a child in it. But there are people in this town who want somebody to be punished, and he is somebody.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: He'll have bread and a blanket and the bucket. Nobody is to say Hale is a hard man. Here: the bounty the council posted for the books. It isn't much. Take it before I think better of it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (From the cell, a very small voice: "The man with the keys has a LOT of doors.")

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (Past one in the morning. The Watch House door opens without anyone opening it. Captain Hale comes out in his nightshirt and his boots, eyes closed, lantern unlit. He turns up the lane toward the mine road and does not look at you.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (asleep) Seven. Eight. Door's open, Fitch. Door's open. Somebody ought to shut it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (He walks like a man being gently pulled on a string.)

options.text: Follow close, the whole way, and note the road.
Watch from the lane and see where he goes.
Take his arm and wake him.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (You keep a dozen paces back. He does not take the mine road at all, as you thought he would.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (At the last lantern he turns off across the Briarwood by a line of trampled ferns, a path nobody walks awake, and the roots do not trip him. Far ahead, between two leaning stones, the air goes cold.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (At the Bell Line stones he stops. He sways. His hand comes up as if to a knocker that is not there.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (Then, as if someone had said no, he turns, and walks all the way home by the same ferns, and you walk behind him, and the map of it is in your head.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (at his own door, still asleep) Not that way. Never that way. Whose door is that?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (You keep to the shadow of the lantern posts. He goes up the lane, past the forge and the Ox, and up the mine road with his shirt tail flapping, a grey man in grey light.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (At the Bell Line stones he stops, sways, and turns back as if someone had said no.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (In the morning his boots will be dusty to the ankle, and he will not know why.)

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (You take his arm. He comes up out of sleep like a man out of cold water, and stands in the road in his nightshirt, looking at his boots.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: What am I... Why am I in the road? ...Oh. Oh, no. Not again. Not with someone watching.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I tie my laces to the bedpost. Did you know? I tie them tight, and in the morning they are still tied, and my boots are on the other side of the door. Don't tell. Please.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (Juniper has walked over with you, a flask in each hand and the face of a woman who would sooner be anywhere with a wolf in it.)

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Wakeful tea, Captain. Bellwort, mint, and something I won't name, because you'd ask for the recipe. One cup before bed. It keeps your head on the pillow and your feet in the bed.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (drinking) It tastes of boots. Which I suppose is fair.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: It's meant to. Drink it.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Juniper. You came to the Watch House. On your own feet, in daylight. And you haven't mentioned a wolf once.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: I'm told I'm very sensible. I'd rather be useful.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: (The little blue bottle. Half the town swears by it.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Sleep. Proper sleep. I'd almost forgotten it had a taste, like warm bread. Thank you, truly. I'll sleep like the dead tonight.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: With my say-so. Yes. Yes, all right. Not the laces. Me. You'll tie it loose enough to breathe and tight enough to argue with.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: And you'll be there to untie it at dawn, or I'll have the lads do it, and they'll talk. The dignity of the Watch is a fragile thing.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: A bell. Fitch had one over the Ox's cellar door; it rang at all the wrong moments. Aye. The Watch's hand-bell, from the shelf by the kettle. If it rings and I'm not up, the lads come.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: If it rings and the lads are asleep, heaven help the town. Hang it. I'll sleep to the sound of it, or I won't.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: You mean to walk it with me. Every step. In the ferns, in the dark, behind a man in his shirt.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Aye. All right. Mark the way, and keep a clear head; there is a place on it that I don't like. Better that someone knows where I go than nobody.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: That is more than I would ask of a stranger. If the council knew, Vane would have the Watch by Sunday and I'd have a chair by the fire.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: You've my thanks, and what's left of my knees. If it comes to the council, I'll stand with you, whatever it costs me.
